stem: A body initially at rest explodes into three fragments. Two of the fragments have equal mass and fly off with equal speeds in opposite directions. The third fragment will: (a) remain at rest (b) start moving in the direction of either fragment (c) move perpendicular to the direction of motion of the other two (d) move with zero momentum —
The area of F-t curve is A, where 'F' is the force on one mass due to the other. If one of the colliding bodies of mass M is at rest initially, then its speed just after the collision is _____. —
A cannon on friction-less ground fires a shell with muzzle velocity 'u' as shown (barrel at 60° to the ground, cannon mass M, shell mass m). Calculate the recoil speed of the cannon. —
A man of mass 50 kg jumps off a 100 kg plank lying on a frictionless floor. His velocity w.r.t. the plank is 4 m/s. Calculate the recoil speed of the plank. —

A system of two blocks A (mass 3m) and B (mass m) are connected by an inextensible massless string over a massless, frictionless pulley. Initially the system is at rest. A bullet of mass 'm' moving with velocity 'u' hits block B and gets embedded into it. Find the impulse imparted by the tension force to the block of mass 3m. —

key: c move in opposite directions with equal speeds
stem: A particle at rest suddenly disintegrates into two particles of equal masses which start moving. The two fragments will: (a) move in the same direction with equal speeds (b) move in any direction with any speed (c) move in opposite directions with equal speeds (d) move in opposite directions with unequal speeds —
A shell explodes and many pieces fly off in different directions. Which of the following is conserved? (a) Kinetic energy (b) Momentum (c) Neither momentum nor KE (d) Momentum and KE —

key: b The kinetic energy but not the linear momentum
stem: Internal forces can change: (a) The linear momentum but not the kinetic energy (b) The kinetic energy but not the linear momentum (c) Linear momentum as well as kinetic energy (d) Neither the linear momentum nor the kinetic energy —

key: c in opposite directions with equal speeds
stem: A body at rest breaks into two pieces of equal masses. The parts will move: (a) in same direction (b) a long different lines (c) in opposite directions with equal speeds (d) in opposite directions with unequal speeds —

A bullet in motion hits and gets embedded in a solid block resting on a frictionless table. Which of the following is conserved? (a) Momentum and KE (b) Kinetic energy alone (c) Neither KE nor momentum (d) Momentum alone —

key: 5/3 m/s, in the direction of the 2 kg block's motion
stem: Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 1 kg are placed on a frictionless horizontal surface, as shown in the figure (2 kg moving at 5 m/s to the right, 1 kg moving at 5 m/s to the left, 4 m apart). Find the speed and direction of motion of the centre-of-mass (c.o.m.) particle of the system. —

A uranium 238 nucleus, initially at rest, emits an alpha particle with speed of 1.17 × 10⁷ m/s. Calculate the recoil speed of the residual nucleus thorium 234. Assume the mass of a nucleus is proportional to its mass number. If the recoil speed (in m/s) is given by x × 10⁵, find the value of x. —

Bullets of mass 10 g each are fired from a machine gun at a rate of 60 bullets/minute. The muzzle velocity of the bullets is 100 m/s. The thrust force due to firing bullets experienced by the person holding the gun stationary is _____ (in N). —

key: d both move in opposite directions but α-particle with greater speed
stem: A nuclide at rest emits an α-particle. In this process: (a) α-particle moves with large velocity and the nucleus remains at rest (b) both α-particle and nucleus move with equal speed in opposite directions (c) both move in opposite directions but nucleus with greater speed (d) both move in opposite directions but α-particle with greater speed —
A bomb of mass 9 kg explodes into two pieces of masses 3 kg and 6 kg. The velocity of mass 3 kg is 16 m/s. The KE of mass 6 kg (in joule) is: (a) 96 (b) 384 (c) 192 (d) 768 —

Two trolleys A and B are free to move on a level frictionless track, and are initially stationary. A man on trolley A throws a bag of mass 10 kg with a horizontal velocity of 4 m/s with respect to himself onto trolley B of mass 100 kg. The combined mass of trolley A (excluding bag) and the man is 140 kg. Find the ratio of velocities of trolleys A and B, just after the bag lands on trolley B. —

Velocity of a particle of mass 2 kg varies with time t according to the equation v⃗ = (2t î + 4ĵ) m/s. Here t is in seconds. Find the impulse imparted to the particle in the time interval from t = 0 to t = 2 s ⚠ (in m/s) .

A spacecraft of mass M moves with velocity V in free space at first, then it explodes breaking into two pieces. If after explosion a piece of mass m comes to rest, the other piece of spacecraft will have a velocity: (a) MV/(M−m) (b) MV/(M+m) (c) mV/(M−m) (d) mV/(M+m) —

key: b Only one part will follow parabolic path
stem: A body just dropped from a tower explodes into two pieces of equal mass in mid-air. Which of the following is not possible? (a) Each part will follow parabolic path (b) Only one part will follow parabolic path (c) Both parts move along a vertical line (d) One part reaches the ground earlier than the other —

A man of mass M stands at one end of a plank of length L which lies at rest on a frictionless surface. The man walks to the other end of the plank. If the mass of the plank is M/3, then the distance that the man moves relative to ground is: (a) 3L/4 (b) L/4 (c) 4L/5 (d) L/3 —

A (trolley + child) of total mass 200 kg is moving with a uniform speed of 36 km/h on a frictionless track. The child of mass 20 kg starts running on the trolley from one end to the other (10 m away) with a speed of 10 ms⁻¹ relative to the trolley in the direction of the trolley's motion, and jumps out of the trolley with the same relative velocity. How much has the trolley moved from the time the child begins to run (in metre)? —

During a heavy rain, hailstones of average size 1.0 cm in diameter fall with an average speed of 20 m/s. Suppose 2000 hailstones strike every square metre of a 10 m × 10 m roof perpendicularly in one second and assume that the hailstones do not rebound. Calculate the average force exerted by the falling hailstones on the roof. Density of hailstones is 900 kg/m³, take π = 3.14 (in N). —

After scaling a wall of 3 m height a man of weight W drops himself to the ground. If his body comes to a complete stop 0.15 sec after his feet touch the ground, calculate the average impulsive force in the vertical direction exerted by the ground on his feet (g = 9.8 m/s²) (in W). —

Two particles having position vectors r⃗₁ = (3î + 5ĵ) metres and r⃗₂ = (−5î − 3ĵ) metres are moving with velocities v⃗₁ = (4î + 3ĵ) m/s and v⃗₂ = (aî + 7ĵ) m/s. If they collide after 2 seconds, the value of 'a' is: (a) 2 (b) 4 (c) 6 (d) 8 —

A stationary body explodes into two fragments of masses m₁ and m₂. If momentum of one fragment is p, the energy of explosion is: (a) p²/(2(m₁+m₂)) (b) p²/(2√(m₁m₂)) (c) p²(m₁+m₂)/(2m₁m₂) (d) p²/(2(m₁−m₂)) —

A railway flat car has an artillery gun installed on it. The combined system has a mass M and moves with a velocity v₀. The barrel of the gun makes an angle α with the horizontal. A shell of mass m leaves the barrel at a speed u relative to the barrel in the forward direction. The speed of the flat car so that it may stop after the firing is: (a) mu/(M+m) (b) (Mu/(M+m)) (c) mu cosα/(M+m) (d) (M+m)α cosα —

A man weighting 80 kg is standing at the centre of a flat boat and he is 20 m from the shore. He walks 8 m on the boat towards the shore and then halts. The boat weighs 200 kg. How far is he from the shore at the end of this time? (a) 11.2 m (b) 13.8 m (c) 14.3 m (d) 15.4 m —

A spaceship of speed v₀ travelling along +y axis suddenly shoots out one fourth of its part with speed 2v₀ along +x axis. xy axes are fixed with respect to the ground. The velocity of the remaining part is: (a) (2/3)v₀ (b) (√20/3)v₀ (c) (√5/3)v₀ (d) (√13/3)v₀ —

A buggy of mass 100 kg is free to move on a frictionless horizontal track. Two men, each of mass 50 kg, are standing on the buggy, which is initially stationary. The men jump off the buggy with velocity = 10 m/s relative to the buggy. In one situation, the men jump one after the other. In another situation, the men jump simultaneously. What is the ratio of the recoil velocities of the buggy in the two cases? (a) 5:4 (b) 5:3 (c) 7:6 (d) 7:5 —

A boy of mass 60 kg is standing over a platform of mass 40 kg placed over a smooth horizontal surface. He throws a stone of mass 1 kg with velocity v = 10 m/s at an angle of 45° with respect to the ground. Find the displacement of the platform (with boy) on the horizontal surface when the stone lands on the ground (in cm). (g = 10 m/s²) —

key: d 4√2 m/s at 135° from each body
stem: A body at rest breaks up into 3 parts. If 2 parts having equal masses fly off perpendicularly each with a velocity of 12 m/s, then the velocity of the third part which has 3 times mass of each part is: (a) 4√2 m/s at an angle of 45° from each body (b) 24√2 m/s at an angle of 135° from each body (c) 6√2 m/s at 135° from each body (d) 4√2 m/s at 135° from each body —

A shell is fired from a cannon with a velocity V at an angle θ with the horizontal direction. At the highest point in its path, it explodes into two pieces of equal masses. One of the pieces retraces its path to the cannon. The speed of the other piece immediately after the explosion is: (a) 3V cosθ (b) 2V cosθ (c) (3/2)V cosθ (d) V cosθ —

A skater of mass m standing on ice throws a stone of mass M with a velocity of v m/s in a horizontal direction. The distance over which the skater will move back (the coefficient of friction between the skater and the ice is μ) is: (a) M²v²/(2mμg) (b) Mv²/(2m²μg) (c) M²v²/(2m²μg) (d) M²v²/(2m²μ²g) —

Two blocks of masses m and M are moving with speeds v₁ and v₂ (v₁ > v₂) in the same direction on a frictionless surface, with M being ahead of m. An ideal spring of force constant k is attached to the backside of M. The maximum compression of the spring when the blocks collide is: (a) v₁√(m/k) (b) v₂√(M/k) (c) (v₁−v₂)√(mM/((M+m)k)) (d) None of these —

A particle of mass 3m is projected from the ground at some angle with horizontal. The horizontal range is R. At the highest point of its path it breaks into two pieces m and 2m. The smaller mass comes to rest and the larger mass finally falls at a distance x from the point of projection where x is equal to: (a) 3R/4 (b) 3R/2 (c) 5R/4 (d) 3R —

A ball of mass m is released from A inside a smooth wedge of mass m as shown in the figure (A is on the rim of a circular groove of radius R, level with the centre O; the ball is shown further down the arc at B, where OB makes 45° with the vertical through the lowest point; the wedge rests on a smooth floor). What is the speed of the wedge when the ball reaches point B? —

A 5.0 g bullet moving at 100 m/s strikes a log. Assume that the bullet undergoes uniform deceleration and stops in 6.0 cm. Find (i) the time taken for the bullet to stop, (ii) the impulse on the log and (iii) the average force experienced by the log. —

A 3.0 kg block slides on a frictionless horizontal surface, first moving to the left at 50 m/s. It collides with a spring as it moves left, compresses the spring and is brought to rest momentarily. The body continues to be accelerated to the right by the force of the compressed spring. Finally, the body moves to the right at 40 m/s. The block remains in contact with the spring for 0.020 s. What were the magnitude and direction of the impulse of the spring on the block? What was the spring's average force on the block? —

The net force versus time graph of a rocket is shown in the figure (F rises linearly from 0 to 20 kN over t = 0 to 2 s, stays constant at 20 kN from t = 2 s to t = 10 s, then falls linearly from 20 kN to 0 from t = 10 s to t = 16 s). The mass of the rocket is 1200 kg. Calculate the velocity of the rocket 16 seconds after starting from rest. Neglect gravity. —
